articles.fullText:
China on Thursday called on the international community to find a home for the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) best positioned for its efficient operation, pointing out problems with the joint candidature by Belgium and Chile.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing after Belgium and Chile on Nov. 6 announced the decision to join their candidatures for the seat of the secretariat. This joint candidature provides for the secretariat being based in the city of Valparaíso, Chile, the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM) will be installed in and operating from Brussels, and Brussels will host the meetings of the subsidiary bodies.
Mao said that earlier this year, China nominated Xiamen to bid for the seat of the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement, noting that the candidature has quickly received the support of the majority of the Parties to the Agreement.
"By seeking an unauthorized backroom deal on issues that should be determined by the Conference of the Parties (COP), the joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects," the spokesperson said.
First, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement. According to the agreement, the seat of the secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the CHM, including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by COP, and the CHM shall be managed by the secretariat, she said.
"Belgium and Chile traded under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties to the Agreement. This is a violation of the stipulations of the agreement and an act of disrespect to the authority of COP," Mao said.
Second, it contravenes procedural justice, Mao said, adding that the choice of the secretariat seat and the development of the CHM are two items of different nature scheduled to be collectively determined by COP through separate decisions.
The Belgium-Chile proposal bundles the two together in an attempt to force it as a package upon other Parties, which is against applicable procedural rules and a hijack of the Parties' will, she said.
Third, it contravenes established international practice. Stressing that the management of the CHM is a key mandate of the secretariat, Mao said in the practice established by other international treaties like the Convention on Biological Diversity, the secretariats and CHMs are located in the same place.
"The Belgium-Chile proposal, which locates the Secretariat and the CHM separately across the ocean, will without a doubt raise the operation cost, lower management efficiency, and increase the financial burden on the Parties to the Agreement," Mao said.
Fourth, it contravenes equitable geographical distribution. The vast majority of major global institutions are based in Europe, with none located in Asia. Developing countries have been calling on global institutions to redress this long-existing injustice and bring about greater fairness and equity, the spokesperson said.
She said Brussels is already home to the headquarters of NATO and the EU. "If this non-coastal city were to host the CHM of an ocean-related treaty as well, it would further widen the digital divide to the detriment of the shared interests of the Global South."
Fifth, it contravenes fair competition. Noting the BBNJ Secretariat is tasked with contributing to global ocean governance, and the selection of its seat should be a fair and friendly process in keeping with the rules, Mao said the Belgium-Chile proposal, however, politicizes the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps.
"It not only undermines the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of multilateralism," she said.
Sixth, it contravenes the original commitment. Chile first made the bid citing its significance for the Global South. Yet according to the new proposal, Chile will no longer assume the substantive functions of the secretariat. Belgium, for its part, only seeks to host the CHM and thereby has in effect relinquished its bid for the secretariat seat, Mao said.
Stressing that the adoption and entry into force of the BBNJ Agreement is a victory of multilateralism, Mao said its implementation likewise needs to serve and advance the common well-being of all humanity.
"We call on the international community to find a home for the secretariat best positioned for its efficient operation and the effective implementation of the agreement," Mao said, adding that China firmly supports multilateralism and the cause of the UN, and is committed to promoting and improving global ocean governance.
She said that as one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China has the will, capability and confidence to provide strong support and backing for the operation of the secretariat.
"China is full ready. We look forward to working with all Parties to the Agreement to keep the selection of the secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, and uphold the overall and fundamental interests of the international community, especially those of developing countries," Mao said.

As autumn gives way to winter, respiratory infections become more common, and early symptoms such as coughing and fever can easily be mistaken for a seasonal cold. But pneumonia is far more serious than a bad cold. Observed every year on November 12, World Pneumonia Day highlights the global burden of a disease that remains a major cause of illness and death, with young children, older adults and people with underlying health conditions particularly vulnerable.
According to the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), more than 725,000 children under five still die from pneumonia each year, including about 190,000 newborns. In China, older adults, children and people with chronic diseases remain the key groups for respiratory disease protection.
In recent years, China has strengthened its approach to respiratory disease prevention and control, with vaccination serving as the first line of defense and primary-level healthcare networks providing a safety net.
At a news conference in November 2025 on the prevention and control of acute respiratory infectious diseases during the autumn and winter seasons, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration called on key groups, including older adults, people with underlying health conditions and children, to receive influenza and pneumococcal vaccines.
During peak respiratory disease seasons, the tiered diagnosis and treatment system handles routine triage: community health centers and township health centers guide patients with mild symptoms to seek nearby care or recover at home, prioritizing emergency resources for severe cases to reduce severe illness and mortality.
A dual emphasis on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Western medicine offers another low-cost, highly accessible path. The strength of TCM techniques lies in regulating body constitution, relieving symptoms and shortening recovery time, while providing sustained support in the stable-phase management of chronic respiratory diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

(ECNS) -- Climate change poses the biggest threat to the vision of ecological civilization, and no country can tackle the global challenge alone, said Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, on Thursday.
Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, made the remarks at the China-Türkiye Dialogue on Ecological Civilization and Green Transition held in Istanbul during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which kicked off on Monday in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya.
The dialogue was hosted by China News Service and the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, with China News Network and the Policy Research Center for Environment and Economy of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (PRCEE) as co-organizers. It's also the second multilateral event of China News Service’s flagship program "News Lounge" held in Türkiye.
Coşar said ecological civilization is, in its broadest sense, a philosophical and political concept aimed at rebuilding the relationship between humanity and nature on the basis of balance and sustainability, in response to the global climate crisis and ecological degradation.
He noted that discussions on ecological civilization, known in Chinese as "shengtai wenming," began in China in the 1980s. In 2018, the concept was incorporated into China's Constitution as a national goal.
Coşar outlined three key features of ecological civilization. First, it rejects a development model that treats humanity as the master of nature and seeks to protect life and biodiversity. Second, it places natural ecological assets and sustainability at the center of economic structures, moving beyond growth models focused primarily on GDP. Third, it represents political and social transformation that integrates socialism with ecological principles, as reflected in China's national strategy.
Addressing the challenges posed by climate change, Coşar said humanity's continued pursuit of a more comfortable lifestyle, along with industrial production, technological development, and warfare, has placed growing pressure on the environment and contributed to greenhouse gas emissions. He noted that while industrialization and technological progress have driven social development, they have also brought significant ecological challenges that should not be overlooked.
The impact of warfare is particularly concerning. Beyond the direct destruction of natural environments and ecosystems, war-related activities also generate substantial emissions, with environmental consequences that may persist for a long time and affect future generations. Climate change, he stressed, is therefore not only a challenge facing today's societies but also a global issue with long-term implications.
Coşar stressed that climate change is a global phenomenon that cannot be addressed by any country acting alone. He also expressed concern that some of the countries contributing most to global pollution are taking the fewest measures to combat climate change.
Coşar concluded by emphasizing that climate change is a long-term and complex global challenge with far-reaching consequences. Given the evolving climate situation, no country can achieve its vision of ecological civilization on its own, making stronger international cooperation essential to advancing ecological civilization worldwide.

The report finds that climate action is becoming more deeply embedded in national policymaking, but projected emissions remain substantially off track from the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius.
Current pledges are expected to reduce emissions by around 6% by 2035 compared with 2019 levels. Even if fully implemented, they would deliver a reduction of only around 9%.
COP31 will need to address this gap between ambition and implementation, ensuring that targets translate into concrete action this decade.
Dawes Glacier in Alaska, the United States. 
Climate finance and adaptation will be another major test. At COP30 in Belém, Brazil, in 2025, countries called for efforts to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035.
They also took forward the Baku-to-Belém Roadmap, outlining a pathway to mobilize at least $1.3 trillion annually for climate action by 2035.
The conference launched the Global Implementation Accelerator and the Belém Mission to 1.5 degrees Celsius to support national climate plans.
Yet the adaptation finance gap remains vast. The UN Environment Programme's Adaptation Gap Report 2026, released on November 4, estimates developing countries will need $305 billion annually for adaptation by 2035.
International public adaptation finance from developed to developing countries stood at just $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in 2024. Even tripling these flows by 2035 would cover only 20 to 29% of the estimated needs.
Terraced fields in Yuanyang County, Yunnan Province, southwest China. 
As COP31 gets underway, negotiators will face pressure to improve access to climate finance, support developing countries and advance a just transition for workers and communities.
Ten years after the Paris Agreement entered into force, the summit will test whether international cooperation can translate commitments into tangible progress.

《联合国气候变化框架公约》第三十一次缔约方大会（COP31）将于周一在土耳其安塔利亚开幕，持续至11月20日。此次峰会面临一个核心挑战：将国家承诺转化为可衡量的减排量，并加大对脆弱国家的支持力度。2026年11月7日，土耳其安塔利亚，COP31蓝区一景。落实是土耳其担任COP31主席国的重点。其2035年目标包括将电力在最终能源需求中的占比从目前的略高于20%提高到35%，并将建筑行业的能源消耗强度至少降低25%。

主席国还寻求推进零废弃物、甲烷减排、粮食安全和绿色工业化。中国南方广西壮族自治区杨村镇的风力涡轮机。一项重大考验将是各国能否缩小其国家气候计划与《巴黎协定》目标之间的差距。《联合国气候变化框架公约》秘书处于10月27日发布的一份综合报告记录，2024年1月至2026年8月期间提交了127份新的国家自主贡献（NDC），代表《巴黎协定》154个缔约方。这些贡献合计覆盖了2019年全球温室气体排放量的约71%（不包括土地利用、土地利用变化和林业）。

土耳其安塔利亚地中海海岸一景。报告发现，气候行动正日益深入地融入国家政策制定，但预计排放量仍严重偏离将全球变暖限制在1.5摄氏度的目标。当前承诺预计到2035年将比2019年水平减少约6%的排放。即使全面实施，也仅能实现约9%的减排。COP31需要解决雄心与落实之间的这一差距，确保目标在本十年转化为具体行动。

美国阿拉斯加道斯冰川。气候融资和适应将是另一项重大考验。2025年在巴西贝伦举行的COP30上，各国呼吁到2035年至少将适应资金增加两倍。他们还推进了《巴库至贝伦路线图》，勾勒出到2035年每年至少动员1.3万亿美元用于气候行动的路径。会议启动了全球实施加速器和贝伦1.5摄氏度使命，以支持国家气候计划。

然而，适应资金缺口依然巨大。联合国环境规划署11月4日发布的《2026年适应差距报告》估计，到2035年发展中国家每年需要3050亿美元用于适应。2024年，发达国家向发展中国家提供的国际公共适应资金仅为282亿至317亿美元。即使到2035年将这些资金流增加两倍，也只能覆盖估计需求的20%至29%。中国西南部云南省元阳县的梯田。

随着COP31的展开，谈判代表将面临压力，需要改善气候融资的获取渠道、支持发展中国家，并推进面向工人和社区的公正转型。《巴黎协定》生效十年后，此次峰会将检验国际合作能否将承诺转化为切实进展。
